summary: Robert Anderson was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Harrow School (~1805–1809) and East India Company College (~1809–1811), where he later served as Assistant Professor from 1821 to 1825.

Robert Anthony Orsi works in religious studies and history/archaeology. Educated at Trinity College, Hartford, and Yale University, he held posts at Fordham, Indiana University Bloomington, Harvard, Northwestern (as Chair of Catholic Studies from ~2007), and Notre Dame (2020–2021).

Robert Antoine was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an M.A. at the University of Calcutta (~1948–1950). He founded Shanti Bhavan in 1950, taught Sanskrit at St. Xavier's Collegiate School (1951), and joined Jadavpur University in 1956.

Robert Arrowsmith worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying at Columbia and Berlin, he taught at Columbia and Racine College, served as principal of Barnard School and Erasmus Hall, was professor at Teachers College, and edited for American Book Company (1894–1913).

Robert Atkinson was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Trinity College Dublin and the University of Liège. He held professorships at Trinity College Dublin (1869) and Trinity College, Hartford (1871–1907), and served as Royal Irish Academy president (1901–1906).

Robert Baker Aitken was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. Educated at the University of Hawaiʻi and UC Berkeley, he trained under D. T. Suzuki and multiple Zen masters, founded the Honolulu Diamond Sangha and Buddhist Peace Fellowship, and held university posts.
Robert Barkley Shaw was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He completed his education at Marlborough College (~1853–1856) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1856–1859).

Robert Barnett is a Tibetology scholar educated at the University of Cambridge. He founded the Tibet Information Network, directed summer programs at Tibet University, and taught at Columbia University (~1999–2018), SOAS, King's College London, Princeton, and INALCO.

Robert Bleichsteiner worked in Tibetology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Bittner, von Schroeder, and Geiger, later serving there as privatdozent and professor, as well as director of Weltmuseum Wien (1945).

Robert Boxberger was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Jena under August Schleicher (1855–1858) and worked as a teacher at Realschule Erfurt (1858–1876) and librarian at Herzogin Anna Amalia Bibliothek (1868–1876).

Robert Brainerd Ekvall worked in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Wheaton College, Nyack College, and the University of Chicago, he held research positions at Chicago, the University of Washington (1958–1964), and the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture (1965–1973).

Robert Bruce Foote was an archaeology and history specialist. He served as Superintendent at the Geological Survey of India (1858–1891), worked for Baroda State in 1892, and became Director of the Mysore Geological Department in 1894.

Robert Caesar Childers was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Wadham College, Oxford, and under Yataramulle Dhammarama, later serving as Sub-Librarian at the India Office (1872) and professor at University College London (1873).

Robert Chalmers was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at City of London School and Oriel College, Oxford, studying under Edwin Abbott Abbott and T. W. Rhys Davids. He served as Royal Asiatic Society president and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge.

Robert Chambers was an Indology and law scholar educated at Oxford. He was Vinerian Professor of English Law at Oxford (1766–1777), Principal of New Inn Hall, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William (~1789–1798), and President of The Asiatic Society.

Robert Charles Zaehner worked in religious studies, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Christ Church, Oxford, and under Harold Walter Bailey at Cambridge, he became Spalding Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics and a fellow of All Souls College, Oxford.
Robert Cotton Mather was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He pursued his education at the University of Edinburgh, the University of Glasgow (~1828–1831), and Homerton College (~1831–1833).

Robert DeCaroli is an art history, Indology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his MA and PhD at UCLA under Robert L. Brown and Katherine Anne Harper, and held posts at UCLA, Loyola Marymount, the Getty Research Institute, and George Mason University.

Robert Deliège is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1980–1983) and held academic posts at the University of Kerala and Université catholique de Louvain (professeur from ~1993).
Robert Drummond was an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh. He served as a surgeon for the East India Company from ~1797 to 1809.
